summary.title: Go WebAssembly Tutorial - Building a Calculator Tutorial
summary.one_liner: You learn how to compile a Go program to WebAssembly with GOARCH=wasm GOOS=js and build a small browser calculator that exposes Go functions to JavaScript and reads and writes DOM elements.
keywords: how to run go in the browser
takeaways: Build a Go program with GOARCH=wasm GOOS=js go build -o lib.wasm and load it in a page using wasm_exec.js and WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming.
Expose Go functions to JavaScript by registering them with js.Global().Set and js.FuncOf, and keep the program alive with a channel.
Read input values from DOM elements with document.getElementById and write results back to the page.
Note that js.NewCallback was used in Go 1.11-1.20 and js.FuncOf is the replacement from Go 1.21 onward.
The tutorial omits error handling for strconv.Atoi and is written for the Go 1.11 era, so it is a starting point rather than production code.
summary.summary: The article walks through compiling Go to WebAssembly, starting with a Hello World that logs to the console. It then shows how to load lib.wasm in a page with wasm_exec.js, serve files with a small net/http server, and register Go add and subtract functions as JavaScript callbacks. The final steps evaluate input element values, parse them with strconv.Atoi, and write results back to the DOM, producing a working calculator. The code is from the Go 1.11 era, with a note updating it for Go 1.12 and later API changes.
